_schema.applies_to: matcher on {program, metrics, subgroups}; null = any
_schema.basis: traceability: docs/replication-assessment.md section, engine metadata recorded in data/pe/pe_meta.json, a GitHub issue, or a measured diagnostic in this repo's data

annotations.text: PolicyEngine values are annual 2024 on the certified Populace artifact; Urban values are average-month 2023. Level differences partly reflect period and vintage, not only model differences.

Urban's participation numerator is the actual administrative caseload divided by ATTIS-simulated eligibles. PolicyEngine's is simulated participation (seeded take-up flags + calibrated weights); for count-targeted programs (SNAP, SSI) the numerator is disciplined by the same class of admin counts, so convergence there is partly by construction.
PolicyEngine's is_snap_eligible includes the full eligibility battery including BBCE categorical eligibility, matching Urban's denominator concept.
annotations.basis: docs/replication-assessment.md §2; engine metadata for is_snap_eligible in data/pe/pe_meta.json

annotations.text: PolicyEngine's native is_ssi_eligible is explicitly 'without income test' — broader than Urban's payable concept. The scorecard instead uses adults with SSI amount > 0 under forced take-up (fullpart run) as the payable denominator, approximating Urban's concept. Child SSI is excluded (Urban's universe is adults 18+).
annotations.basis: docs/replication-assessment.md §2, §7 item 6; engine metadata for is_ssi_eligible; construction measured in data/pe/pe_metrics.json (run=fullpart_urban6)

annotations.text: PolicyEngine has no national income-tested TANF eligibility variable (state-by-state machinery only). The scorecard uses persons in units where TANF pays > 0 under forced take-up as the income-eligible counterpart. TANF dollars on Build P miss the ACF admin total by −36%, so treat TANF comparisons as provisional.

Urban publishes family-level TANF participation with and without solely-state-funded (SSF) programs. PolicyEngine's TANF models the assistance-unit program without an SSF distinction; family-unit rows are not yet computed.
Both sides count children ages 0–4 only; PolicyEngine's WIC eligibility also covers pregnant/postpartum women, excluded here by the age cut on both eligibility and participation.

WIC has zero calibration targets on Build P; the seeded legacy gate floats free. The close match to Urban's national rate (52.8% vs 53.5% in the replication assessment) is coincidence, not anchoring — FNS WIC targets are on the build list.
Populace's national-default state geography has known 2–3x errors for infants in some states (e.g. CA hot, MI cold). State-level infant WIC rows carry that uncertainty.

PolicyEngine's eligible counterpart is tax units with EITC > 0 under forced take-up. Baseline EITC claims are SOI-targeted and include erroneous claims — nationally, claims (≈23.7M) exceed Urban's simulated eligibles (18.4M), one reason Urban publishes no EITC participation rate.
Build P stores no CTC take-up flag; refundable CTC > 0 is the formula outcome with claims and dollars calibrated to SOI. The count is closer to 'claims' than to a pure eligibility simulation.
annotations.basis: docs/replication-assessment.md §3, §5; data/pe/pe_meta.json (no takes_up flag for CTC among stored inputs)

annotations.text: PolicyEngine's housing eligibility is current recipient OR renter at ≤80% of area median income, at the SPM-unit level; Urban uses ≤50% AMI at the household level. PolicyEngine's computed housing assistance dollars also under-deliver vs HUD administrative totals, so participation-side comparisons are provisional.
PolicyEngine has LIHEAP only as state fragments (DC, IL, MA, plus TX CEAP and Riverside County) with no national output. National LIHEAP is on the build list.
PolicyEngine has CCDF only via state child-care subsidy programs and a generic SPM-unit subsidy variable, with no national CCDF coverage. National CCDF is on the build list.

Urban's counterfactual gives every eligible person/household all benefits for which they are eligible (all nine programs). PolicyEngine's headline counterfactual sets every stored take-up flag True plus the WIC gate (exact toggle list recorded in data/pe/pe_meta.json); it cannot add LIHEAP or CCDF (not nationally modeled), and a variant toggling only the six Urban-program flags is also computed to bound the difference.
annotations.basis: Urban slides p.34; data/pe/pe_meta.json runs log; both variants in data/pe/pe_metrics.json

annotations.text: The 2026 column ages the same certified artifact to 2026 under current law as encoded in the engine (input uprating; not re-calibrated to 2026 projections). It exists to show what a live model adds over a fixed-vintage report; Urban's tool publishes 2023 only. Attached only where the interchange run's 2024 value matches this pipeline's within 0.5% (same construction); the interchange 2026 full-participation poverty rows are excluded pending the WIC-gate fix (see RECONCILIATION.md).
annotations.basis: comparison/ FINDINGS.md '2026 column' section; comparison/RECONCILIATION.md #2; construction gate in pipeline/build_comparison.py

annotations.text: Deviations from official or survey-based poverty statistics are expected by construction and are never inherently problematic: Populace corrects survey benefit underreporting (benefit dollars are calibrated to administrative totals that exceed survey-reported amounts), so its poverty rates should differ from — typically sit below — survey-derived rates. Official numbers here are comparators, not truth, and poverty is a permanent calibration holdout: targets come from administrative systems only.
annotations.basis: doctrine 2026-08-02 (Max); docs/replication-assessment.md §3-§4 (admin-dollar calibration; no poverty targets); scorecard_db/relationships.py::never_calibrate

annotations.text: The counterfactuals start from structurally different baselines. PolicyEngine's calibrated baseline already places annual participation near administrative levels (e.g. SNAP ≈91% of annual eligibles — see the SNAP participation row), so forcing the remaining flags adds little; Urban's average-month baseline has participation at admin caseload ÷ eligibles (SNAP 57.5%), leaving far more headroom. The two 'full participation' poverty deltas answer different questions until PolicyEngine publishes average-month semantics.
annotations.basis: measured in this repo (snap participation_rate row vs Urban's); docs/replication-assessment.md §8; average-month semantics tracked in populace#332

annotations.text: PolicyEngine participation is annual-ever (any benefit during 2024) over annual eligibility; Urban's is average-month. Annual-ever rates exceed average-month rates by construction, independent of model quality.

PolicyEngine race categories come from the artifact's stored race variable (categories recorded in data/pe/pe_meta.json); Urban uses ACS-based non-Hispanic groupings with AAPI including Pacific Islanders. Category construction differs; treat subgroup deltas as indicative.
Urban's disability subgroups use the ACS disability questions; PolicyEngine's is_disabled definition is recorded from engine metadata in data/pe/pe_meta.json. The constructions differ.
The Populace artifact carries no metro/non-metro flag; metro-status subgroups are not yet computable.
Earner-presence and citizenship subgroups are computable from the artifact but not yet included in the scorecard pipeline (v1 backlog).
